title: Course 1 Post-Test: Show What You Know
summary: Use what you learned about boards, signals, circuits, and safe connections. Take your time and show how much you remember.

steps.title: Course 1 Knowledge Check
steps.markdownContent: Answer each question to finish Course 1. Think about the ideas you practiced in the lessons.

interactiveConfig.question: What does a microcontroller board do in a robot?
options: Reads inputs and controls outputs using code
interactiveConfig.explanation: The board runs code that reads inputs and controls outputs.

questions.question: What does a microcontroller board do in a robot?
options: Reads inputs and controls outputs using code
questions.explanation: The board runs code that reads inputs and controls outputs.

questions.question: A sensor detects a button press. What is the button press?
questions.explanation: A button gives the board information, so it is an input.

questions.question: Which pin type is best for reading a simple HIGH or LOW signal?
questions.explanation: Digital pins read or send HIGH and LOW signals.

questions.question: What does an analog input help a board measure?
options: Only two states: on or off
questions.explanation: Analog inputs can read a range of values, such as a changing sensor level.

questions.question: Why does an LED need a resistor in its circuit?
options: To limit current and help protect the LED
To make the LED read a button
questions.explanation: A resistor limits current so too much current does not damage the LED.

questions.question: Why do circuit parts need a shared ground?
options: It gives current a common return path
It raises every signal to 5 volts
questions.explanation: A shared ground gives the circuit a common reference and return path.

questions.question: How should you connect a 5V signal to a 3.3V-only input?
options: Use suitable level protection, such as a level shifter
questions.explanation: A 5V signal can damage a 3.3V-only input; use suitable level protection.

questions.question: In a simple robot system, what usually happens after an input is read?
options: Code decides what to do, then an output responds
questions.explanation: The board reads an input, uses code to decide, and controls an output.

learningGoal: Show that you can use Course 1 ideas about boards, inputs, outputs, circuits, and safety.
